questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 45-year-old mentors young staff and volunteers in her barangay. According to Erikson, she is working on:
questions.rationale: Middle adults (40–65) focus on guiding the next generation; young adults on intimacy; older adults on integrity.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 1 Middle adulthood (PDF p. 4)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A 50-year-old cares for her teenage children and her bedridden mother. She belongs to the:
questions.rationale: Middle adults caught between caring for children and aging parents are called the sandwich generation.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 1 Middle adulthood (PDF p. 4)
questions.quote: Many middle adults find themselves in the “sandwich generation," caughtbetweentheresponsibilitiesofcaringfordependentchildrenand thoseofcaringforagingandailingparents.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which is a leading cause of death and injury among young adults?
questions.rationale: Assaults, vehicle accidents and suicide attempts are major causes of mortality in young adults.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 1 Young adulthood (PDF p. 3)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: The normal aging process, without disease, is called:
questions.rationale: Senescence is normal aging; senility is aging with severe mental deterioration; gerontology is the study of aging.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 1 Late adulthood (PDF p. 5)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: "The body is like a machine; its parts wear out and break down." This describes the:
questions.rationale: Wear-and-tear is a biological theory; disengagement, activity and continuity are psychosocial theories.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 1 Theories of aging (PDF p. 5)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A retired teacher joins a hobby club and tutors children to replace her lost work role. This fits which aging theory?
questions.rationale: Activity theory holds that staying active and taking new roles to replace lost ones promotes successful aging.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 1 Theories of aging (PDF p. 6)
questions.quote: One mustconstantly struggle to remain functional and take on new activities toreplacelostone.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: An older adult gradually withdraws from community roles so younger people can take over. This fits the:
questions.rationale: Disengagement theory says people, being mortal, eventually leave their roles in society to suitable replacements.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 1 Theories of aging (PDF p. 5)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Why does an older adult often feel cold even in warm weather?
questions.rationale: Aging thins subcutaneous tissue and impairs vasomotor regulation, so temperature control is poorer.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 1 Late adulthood (PDF p. 6)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: An older client gets dizzy when standing up quickly. This is mainly due to:
questions.rationale: Reduced baroreceptor efficiency raises the risk of postural hypotension; teach slow position changes.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 1 Late adulthood (PDF p. 6)
questions.quote: Decreased efficiency of baroreceptors(receptors that are sensitive to changes in blood pressure). This increases risk for postural hypotension

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Older adults are at greater risk of drug toxicity mainly because of:
questions.rationale: Lower GFR and creatinine clearance slow drug excretion, so drugs accumulate; start low and go slow.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 1 Late adulthood (PDF p. 6)
questions.quote: Thesechanges increase riskto drug toxicity andriskforfluid electrolyte imbalances.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which bathing practice is best for an older adult with dry skin?
options: Bathe every other day with mild soap
questions.rationale: Sebaceous secretions decrease with age; daily bathing and harsh soaps dry the skin further.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Practice Test 1 answers (PDF p. 312)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: An older client finds it hard to follow a low-salt diet because food tastes bland. The main reason is:
questions.rationale: Taste buds and smell decline with age, so older adults tend to add salt; suggest herbs and spices.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Ch. 1 Middle adulthood changes (PDF p. 4)
questions.quote: Diminished taste sensation.This causes decreased appetite to eat,or desire toaddsalttofood.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: An older client says, "I've had a full life, and I'm at peace with what I've done." This shows:
questions.rationale: Ego integrity is viewing life with satisfaction and accepting death; despair is regret and wishing for more time to fix mistakes.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Practice Test 1 (PDF p. 311)
questions.quote: Views life withsenseof wholeness and satisfaction frompast accomplishments.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: When teaching an older adult, the nurse should:
options: Teach everything in one long session
questions.rationale: Short, repeated sessions suit reduced attention span; learning remains possible and decisions stay with the client.
questions.source: Udan, Medical-Surgical Nursing, 2nd ed., Practice Test 1 (PDF p. 311)
